root_cause.summary: simp [bind, Except.bind] unfolds Except.bind over a bind whose scrutinee is the arithmetic-carrying convertToShares call; the emitted proof term obliges the kernel to whnf that scrutinee, and the kernel ignores @[irreducible], so it descends into Operations.mul / Rounding.divideNat / Word.checked / uint256Bound with symbolic arguments and never reaches a constructor.
root_cause.heartbeat_relation: same reduction; 4000/10000 heartbeats -> deterministic timeout, 20000 -> excessive memory

recommendation.R1: Add bindOkGen and bindErrorGen: generic Except bind lemmas proved by rfl at fully abstract {e a b}; kernel then does zero arithmetic per use.
recommendation.R2: deposit_after_drip: replace `simp [bind, Except.bind]` with `exact bindOkGen chi _` after `rw [deposit_def, hchi]`. Verified on the frozen statement.
recommendation.R3: deposit_invalid_zero/_self: drop `simp [bind, Except.bind]`; close with `rw [..., hs, bindOkGen, guardReceiver_zero|guardReceiver_self, bindErrorGen]`, or `simp only [...]` with the same lemmas. Never plain simp with Except.bind.
recommendation.R4: Standing rule for mint/withdraw/redeem/Adapter: never unfold Except.bind while a scrutinee is still an unevaluated convertToShares/convertToAssets/previewMint/previewWithdraw/Operations.*/Word.checked call. Put it in constructor form first (the pattern Conversion.lean already uses) or step the bind with the generic lemmas.
recommendation.R5: Stop pursuing source-level helper abstraction. mintAfterGuard is innocent (rung B) and @[irreducible] gives no kernel protection. `opaque` would stop the kernel but would break convertToShares_ok/_floor; not recommended.
